title: compliance-elevator-qa-and-control-scripts
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, sales-friendly brief + technical QA and control-language crib for SOC2/ISO/HIPAA readiness, data handling commitments, and audit-log phrasing. Target is GTM reps, solutions engineers, and the legal/security reviewer who needs short, repeatable language and the underlying control pointers they can surface during customer conversations.

Audience buckets and one-liners (pick-and-use):
- Developer / Engineering buyer: "Redwood gives you an inference runtime you can deploy in your VPC or our hosted cloud with explicit token-level observability, customer-managed keys, and immutable audit trails — so your app meets security controls without re-architecting."
- Platform / Infra buyer: "We provide a consistent API across hosted, reserved, and private deployments, plus audit logs and key management integrations (KMS/HSM) to satisfy audit evidence needs for SOC2 and ISO assessments."
- Security / Compliance exec: "Redwood operates with SOC2-aligned controls, offers ISO-aligned documentation, and supports HIPAA workloads with covered-entity agreements, data segmentation, and detailed audit logs for forensic and compliance purposes."

Competitive positioning (short, defensible points):
- Versus managed LLM APIs that don’t offer private deploys: emphasize private deployments (VPC & on-prem) + same API + deterministic rollout/testing to reduce migration friction.
- Versus self-hosted inference stacks: emphasize we handle kernel selection, autoscaling, and continuous batching while giving contractual assurances (SLA, DPA) and audit artifacts — less ops overhead.
- Versus other hosted vendors: call out token-level cost/latency visibility and granular audit logging as differentiators for customers who need forensics and billing reconciliation.
- Risk framing: customers choosing vendors without clear audit/log semantics often struggle with eDiscovery, incident investigations, and showing control maturity in audits — we reduce that gap.

Audit-log & evidence language (snippets reps can use):
- "Audit logs: We provide time-stamped, immutable logs containing request metadata (caller identity, route/model/version, input size, timestamp), response metrics (latency, token counts), and routing decisions. Logs are retained per your retention policy and can be exported for forensic analysis."
- "Access controls: Admin and operator actions are logged; role-based access controls (RBAC) are enforced via directory integration (SCIM/SAML) and detailed access logs are available for audits."
- "Key management: We support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations. Encryption-in-transit and encryption-at-rest are enabled by default; for customers using CMKs we can provide key usage evidence."

How we map to common audit requests (quick control map language):
- SOC2: System description + control narrative: "Redwood maintains a System Description document that maps platform components (control plane, serving runtime, telemetry) to common SOC2 criteria; we provide the narrative and supporting logs during readiness assessments."
- ISO27001: Annex A mapping available on request; policies include information classification, encryption, change control, and incident management.
- HIPAA: We can enter a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) for PHI workloads; controls include data segmentation, access logging, breach notification timelines, and staff HIPAA training attestations.

Sales Q&A (short, scriptable answers):
Q: "Do you have SOC2?"
A: "Yes — Redwood maintains SOC2-aligned controls and provides a SOC2 Type II report to customers under NDA/contract after an initial vetting step. If you need report excerpts for procurement, we have a redacted report process."

Q: "Can we host in our VPC / on-prem?"
A: "Yes — Redwood Private supports VPC and an on-prem install option. The same API, model versions, and observability primitives are available so your compliance posture remains consistent between environments."

Q: "What’s in your audit logs?"
A: "Our logs include caller identity, route and model version, request/response sizes, latency, and routing/fallback events. For Dedicated/Private customers we can increase retention and integrate with your SIEM via secure forwarding."

Q: "How do you support HIPAA?"
A: "We will sign a BAA and provide implementation guidance to ensure PHI isolation: private deployments or dedicated capacity, strict RBAC, and audit logs configured for retention and eDiscovery."

Suggested friction-reducing evidence deliverables (for sales to promise):
- Redacted SOC2 Type II report (NDA)
- System Description + control mapping spreadsheet (CSV)
- Sample audit-log export (sanitized) showing fields and retention headers
- KMS usage summary and key rotation policy excerpt
- BAA template and data processing appendix

Negotiable contract snippets (short form):
- Data Processing: "Redwood will process Customer Data only to provide the Service, in accordance with the DPA; Customer retains ownership of Customer Data."
- Audit Access: "Subject to security review and scheduling, Redwood will provide access to audit artifacts (redacted SOC2, control narratives, and log extracts) required to validate controls under an executed NDA/DPA."
- Data Residency: "Where specified in the Order, Redwood will store and process data in the designated region(s)."

Operational commitments we can reasonably promise now:
- Default encryption-at-rest and TLS for in-transit; CMK support for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Immutable, append-only audit logs with configurable retention, exportable to S3 or SIEM.
- RBAC with SCIM/SAML and admin activity logging.
- Incident response timeline and notification commitments in enterprise addenda.

Open/undecided items to resolve with Product/SRE (callouts for internal owners):
- Maximum default audit log retention for hosted customers before premium billing (Product)
- Level of redaction in sample log exports for sales demos (Legal + SRE)
- Template timelines for SOC2 report availability during procurement windows (Security + Legal)

Quick tactical scripts for SDRs/AE to use in prospecting emails:
- Developer angle: "If you want inference with the same dev ergonomics but enterprise-grade controls (RBAC, CMKs, exportable audit logs) — we can spin up a proof-of-concept in your VPC in X weeks. Can we schedule a 20-min tech walkthrough?"
- Security-angle: "We have SOC2-aligned controls, an ISO mapping, and a BAA option for PHI. Happy to share our redacted SOC2 and control narrative under NDA — interested?"

Appendix: Minimal evidence checklist for a typical procurement review (one-liner status we can surface quickly):
- Redacted SOC2 Type II: available (Y/N) -> Y (requires NDA)
- System description document: available -> Y
- Sample audit-log export: available (sanitized) -> Y
- BAA template: available -> Y
- KMS/CMK integration docs: available -> Y

Notes to internal reviewers:
- Keep language sales-friendly but avoid promising full SOC2 reports without Legal/NDAs.
- Tie any specific retention/region promises back to Product for capacity/cost impacts (this is a common procurement hang-up).
- Update the sample log export with SIEM-forwarding examples and an index of fields (SRE owner).

Unresolved questions for next sync:
- What is the exact SLA language for audit log availability and extraction timeframes? (Product + SRE)
- Do we offer a managed log-retention escrow for customers who need multi-year retention beyond our tiered offering? (Pricing + Product)

Bottom line (one-sentence close for the pitch):
Redwood combines production-grade inference with enterprise controls — same API across deployment modes, fine-grained auditability, and contractual artifacts suitable for SOC2/ISO/HIPAA procurement workflows.

Drafted by: Asha Patel (go-to-market) — please review and flag any legal/security redlines or missing technical commits before we publish to the GTM collateral folder.
